title: HANDLING LARGE BLOBS
subtitle: Files, photos and videos belong in object storage, and their bytes should never pass through your application servers.

items: Users upload or download files larger than a few megabytes.
Media needs processing after upload (thumbnails, transcoding).
Pushing gigabytes through your API servers wastes their bandwidth and memory and fails on long uploads.
The API hands out a presigned URL; the client uploads directly to S3 (multipart: parallel, resumable chunks). Metadata is recorded separately.
S3 event notifications trigger processing (thumbnails, transcoding) and flip status to READY. Don't trust the client to say it finished.
Downloads come from a CDN (or presigned GET URLs), never through the app servers.
Upload with presigned URLs directly to object storage.
Use multipart upload for anything big: parallel, resumable chunks.
Store metadata (owner, status, size, checksum) in a database, separate from the bytes.
React to storage events to start processing; mark the item ready only when done.
Serve downloads through a CDN or presigned GET URLs.

blocks.text: "The API only hands out a presigned multipart URL; the client uploads straight to S3. An S3 event triggers processing, and the file shows as ready when processing finishes."

items: Streaming file bytes through API servers.
Trusting the client to report that an upload completed.

blocks.text: Used in: Video platform (YouTube), File storage and sync (Dropbox), Photo sharing (Instagram)
